This is one of the bestJackboxes. If you're looking for your 2nd or 3rd party pack, this isn't a bad one to pick up. It's one of the ones my friends return to the most. Let's go through each game in the pack!

[b]Trivia Murder Party 2[/b] is an improvement over the original while still keeping the core gameplay feeling exactly the same. The biggest differences you'll see here is more games, and the end sequence requiring a perfect answer for the final escape question.

[b]Joke Boat[/b] is another one we keep coming back to. You write short jokes (with help from prompts) and then it gets compared to another joke someone else wrote, and everyone else votes on which joke was better. It initially sounds like something that would give me creative anxiety, but the jokes are very prompt heavy and structured. First you'll choose between a few joke beginnings, then choose between a few subjects that fit that beginning. Then you write the final part of the joke yourself. Sometimes you get stuck with a difficult setup/subject combination and that's all part of the fun! In the final round, you get the chance to re-write each others jokes.

[b]Role Models[/b] is the third game we regularly come back to. It's best played with people you know well. Everyone will vote on a category, and then you'll be given a list of roles within that category and you'll have to sort your friends into each of those roles. For example, who is the brains, the muscle, the "guy at the computer," etc. You'll get points for accurately predicting who should go where. You can even "double down" on a specific person you think is [i]sure[i/] to get a specific role. There are also tie breaking games, and those will happen a lot. The person with the most points at the end wins!

[b]Push The Button[/b] is kind of like Among Us where one (or a few) of you is an alien aboard a spaceship, and the rest are humans. You'll play a series of games where the humans are given one prompt and the alien(s) is given a very slightly different prompt. If someone thinks someone is an alien, they can push the button to call a vote on whether or not to send them out of the airlock, but each player is only allowed to push the button once! The humans win if they successfully the alien(s) out of the airlock, and lose if they run out of time, or if all humans have pushed the button and there is still at least one alien remaining. This game won't be for everyone (people who don't like lying games), but it does what it does very well.

[b]Dictionarium[/b] is kind of the stinker of the pack, in our opinion. Every Jackbox party pack seems to have at least one, and for this pack, it is this one. Still 4 out of 5 good games is pretty good!
This is kind of like the classic dictionary game people used to play on a rainy day, but with made up words. Players will invent definitions for a made up word that the game presents to you. Then, everyone votes on the best definition, and you get points for everyone that voted for yours. There is a second round where you invent made up words that are synonyms to the definitions you made in the previous rounds, and then a third round where you use those words in a sentence. Whoever has the most points at the end wins.
One of the reasons this game falls so flat on its face is that you can make a word with absolutely no context mean pretty much anything, so the entire first round plays exactly the same no matter what the word is. The second round is just voting on whoever made the best jibberish word, which doesn't even [i]sound[/i] fun. The third round is the one that has the most potential for creativity and to actually have fun with it and maybe make someone laugh, but by this point you're so bored of this game you want it to end.

All in all, this is one of the better packs!

I've had the opportunity to play a TON more Party Pack 6 since I wrote this review, and... honestly, I've come around on it in a pretty major way!

Trivia Murder Party 2 is one of the best trivia games in a Party Pack, giving enough consistent laughs while also being interesting trivia is a hard thing to achieve but TMP2 drives player engagement just as much as it rewards for knowing the correct answers.

Dictionarium, as it turns out, is a lot more fun when you're not stuck playing with a group of racists! Funny how that works. Absolutely not an s-tier game, but it's the kind of solid fun that's worth playing every now and again.

Joke Boat is another mid-tier game. Not the brightest raw joke-telling game (you always have Quiplash for that), but regardless still a good experience most of the time. The little tag-lines you make at the start of the game can sometimes be funnier than the jokes you write, but that just makes reading 'em out after the fact add a little comedic "umph" to your bit.

I don't know how I could have been "indifferent" on Role Models before!!! It's one of my favorite jackbox games all-together, now. I think that some of the categories are *really* interesting, and it's a lot of fun seeing how your friends think of you. S-tier, at least in my book!

Push the Button is still a really good time, but I only ever bother to play it with a full room of 10 (something that is ultimately not that common!!!). However, when you *do* manage to get those full rooms, it's a treat for sure. One of my favorites.

Two years on from my last review, I've played this pack enough to switch my review from a "meh" at best to an absolute positive. These games rock!

The Jackbox Party Pack 6 is a carnival of comedy, a digital funhouse of hilarious mini-games that'll turn your living room into a laughter factory. It's the ultimate catalyst for memorable game nights with friends and family.

"Trivia Murder Party 2" is the twisted trivia game that brings a mix of murder mystery and general knowledge to the table. You'll be answering questions and racing against death, with every wrong answer sending you to a hilariously spooky fate. It's like a haunted game show where the stakes are your virtual life, and it's an absolute scream.

"Role Models" takes the idea of putting labels on people to a whole new level. You'll be assigning your friends to various quirky categories, and the results are bound to uncover hidden truths and absurd stereotypes. It's a revealing experience that'll leave you in stitches.

"Dictionarium" is the word game that encourages you to get creative with language. You'll be inventing wacky definitions for made-up words and voting for your favorites. It's a linguistic playground, and your imagination knows no bounds.

"Joke Boat" is a comedy competition where you'll be writing your own stand-up material and performing it for your virtual audience. It's like trying out your material at an open mic night, with the added bonus of competing against your friends for the biggest laughs.

And "Push the Button" is the ultimate game of deception and deduction. One of your friends is a secret alien, and the rest of the group must work together to figure out who it is before the ship is lost in space. It's a test of your ability to trust, lie, and detect deception, and it's a cosmic rollercoaster.

The beauty of The Jackbox Party Pack 6 is that all you need is a smartphone or tablet to join in on the fun. It's the great equalizer where everyone can be a trivia master, a label-maker, a wordsmith, a comedian, and a detective.

Be prepared for revelations about your friends, outrageous definitions, and stand-up performances that rival your favorite comedians. The laughter will be so infectious that you'll start thinking your friends are the funniest people on the planet.

So, if you're ready for a night of trivia and treachery, hilarious labels, wordplay, stand-up comedy, and interstellar deception, The Jackbox Party Pack 6 is your golden ticket to comedic paradise. Assemble your squad, embrace the absurd, and get ready for an unforgettable evening of digital hilarity.

While no game is perfect, Jackbox Party Pack 6 is, at its core, everything I think I could want from the concept of a game: a deep story, told artfully, able to be engaged at multiple levels; gameplay loops which feel organic and meaningful, but with a sort of lightness to them that keeps you from having to feel frantic or burdened with tedium; eclectic design which is at once soulful and unique, yet still entirely approachable; lively writing which truly brings characters to life as unique individuals, warts and all, completely avoiding even the whiff of them being two-dimensional tropes-on-legs; a thoughtful meshing of its elements which helps the game feel like a true gestalt, rather than in any way a discombobulated frankengame; and--one which few games really can reliably, if ever, accomplish--the ability to create a panoply, a full spectrum, of thought-provoking and emotional moments for the player.

People in other reviews warn you that you will cry. They are correct. You may even ugly-cry, possibly repeatedly. But it will be a good kind, a cathartic kind, an almost startlingly real kind. A kind that most video games can only hope they might ever evoke, if they even deign to try. Even now I mist up a bit in recollection, which is impressive, for a story told about imaginary anthropomorphic spirits of people I've never actually had in my physical life.

I encourage you to visit the game's website and/or check out the artbook, which is something I don't think I've said about any game before. There are layers and threads to the game which quite subtly underlie the game (but deftly, in a way that you don't feel an inexplicable hunch that you're missing them), yet when revealed for what they truly were (as both of the above may do for you in ways the game might not), can be seen in every corner of its grand tapestry. I cannot emphasize enough how much this short, simple, mostly-not-difficult game is a sleeper masterclass in storytelling.

Others have complained about the platformer elements of the game, and these complaints are valid: the combination of camera dynamics, control schema, ability functionality, and level designs can make some parts of the game's platforming frustratingly particular. I'm not sure if this was in some way meant to be metaphorical, however, knowing what I do now about the game's deeper themes. Still, I could've enjoyed the playing of the game more without those issues--but I hope these reservations do not deter a single soul from experiencing this unique gem, because they are naught more than scuff marks.

A certain amount of "grinding" may also be necessary for completion, depending on how you go about playing the game. However, you cannot mess up the game beyond repair (this was likely intentional), so at worst, you might have to take more time than would otherwise be necessary, secondary to choices you make--but it is always still salvageable. The game will never blockade you permanently from anything crucial; at the very worst, you might miss out on a few vignettes.

While you can also tarry as long as you'd like, doing this and that (again, also likely an intentional design choice, in retrospect), the "necessary" content of the game is also fairly short; my fairly thorough playthrough still clocked under 30 hours. Whether you could or would experience replay value is entirely up to you; some stories, after all, are worth experiencing more than once. You would be hard-pressed to find an unequivocally more artful story, told as a game, than this one.

With that in mind, I believe the value for the cost is certainly there--but even if you feel you should get the game on sale, do not miss out on experiencing it, one way or another. It is rare that I can say this about any game, but I absolutely can about Jackbox Party Pack 6: I firmly believe it will enrich the lives of many, if not most, who play it.

Trivia Murder Party 2: A new rendition of the classic trivia game. Sure, there is a trivia element, especially in the finale where the trivia really matters for victory, but much of it is less reliant on trivia, as you can survive and do well without necessarily getting many questions right just by doing well on Jackbox-like minigames. While I am a trivia fan, I appreciate how it is fair to those who are not as big trivia buffs.

Joke Boat: Honestly not a huge fan. There are some elements that are fun, but a huge part of the game is writing punchlines to often very limiting prompts, some of which make little sense. Expect them to devolve into either dad jokes or potty jokes. If that's your type of humor, you might enjoy it. If not, pass on this one.

Role Models: I find this one pretty fun. It's certainly fairly niche, but fun to crack out once in a while. Basically has your friends take Buzfeed quizzes for you, which I find an interesting concept. The execution is decent, though it isn't anything amazing.

Dictionarium: I find this one quite entertaining. Basically, it's like telephone with fake words. You're given a definition, you have to create a new word, then your friends give definitions to it, then they create synonyms based on those new definitions. Lots of room for different kinds of humor, so fun to play with many groups of people.

Push the Button: Basically an alternative to Among Us. The impostors don't really go around killing people. Instead, everyone does "tasks," and people mark others as suspicious based on their performance of those tasks. Impostors will get different prompts. However, they can also sabotage either to give crewmates different prompts or to give themselves more correct prompts. You also have to vote out all the impostors at once, which makes the stakes somewhat higher to be correct.

In general, Party Pack 6 is quite fun in many respects, with many classic games, but also a couple more mediocre or limited games. I really enjoy it because it has some of the games I return to most often (e.g., Trivia Murder Party 2), but I can also see how others may not find the game selection as good.

For me personally, the weakest installment in the series.

I really like the Jackbox series. Just as Knowledge is Power, it is a party game with lots of fun, silly animations and a high replay value. 

Unlike Knowledge is Power however, Jackbox is a little bit more versatile. Instead of being bound to your PlayStation and your smartphone, you can now use your phone or your pc/laptop to connect to jackbox.tv, and play. The connection and overall stability of the game is also a lot better.

There are many Party Packs for the Jackbox games. Each pack offers a set of minigames that you can complete with your company of friends or family. Most of them revolve around choosing the funniest answer, predict who might have answered a certain question in a certain way, or, in general, just who made the most ridiculous drawing. Throughout the mini games, players score points, the player with the most points wins. Easy and simple. 

Of all the Jackbox Party Packs, I thought this one was a little disappointing. 
In this Pack, you can play The Joke Boat, in which you complete lame one liners with your own response. The problem with this game is that the responses never match or resemble any kind of fun. Maybe it is intentional, but when playing with a group, we always skip this one. 

Then you have Trivia Murder Party 2, in which you need to complete a series of very hard mini games, and try to stay alive and be the first to escape the mansion. This one is my personal favorite of this Party Pack and we almost only play this game when launching The Jackbox Party Pack 6. 

Another lame game, in my opinion, is The Dictionarium, in which you must come up with funny definitions of a certain word. For me/us, this just did not work out and the lolz were nowhere to be found.

Another fun game was Push the Button, a Among Us style mini game, in which you need to complete various mini games and uncover the hidden alien on board. Along with Trivia Murder Party 2, this one was my favorite and we switched back and forth between them.

Lastly, you got Role Models, some kind of personally test in which you create some kind of formula about yourself. This one was the most disappointing and did not offer any fun. 

The animations and art style of The Jackbox Party Pack 6 is colorful, jolly and silly. My biggest compliment here, is that all animations and slides within the games, are really fast, keeping the pace of the game at a very healthy levels.

The silly sounds, the jolly music in the background, enhances the experience and lets you have a good time with the game. In the sixth installment in the series, the music and sound in the Trivia Murder Party 2 game, is especially good.

With the right company, I can get aches in my stomach from laughing and I think that The Jackbox Party Packs are the best party games out there by far.

Okay so this pack is normally seen as one of the most mediocre packs, but I think it's better suited as more "hit or miss" rather than mediocre. The overall game quality seems to rely more on the individual players, rather than having an overall consensus.

[h1] Trivia Murder Party 2 [/h1]

Okay so this is my most played jackbox game... ever. You answer trivia questions and getting them right provides you with money, whereas getting them wrong sends you to the killing room. There you play a randomly selected minigame, if you preform poorly you die. The game continues until there's only one player left alive, with dead players still playing for money in the mean time. Then all players are sent to the final round, where they're now given "select all that apply" questions instead of "which is right." Choosing correctly moves you forward a space, the player in first at any given time will be brought back to life, killing whoever they overtook. Whoever was originally alive starts much farther ahead, but they lose out on the third option exclusive to ghosts. I've played this game to the point where I'm not always eager to play it, but I still love it nontheless. (Also the theming is great, just wanted to point that out.)

9/10

[h1] Role Models [/h1]

You pick a topic (i.e. Star Wars characters) and you select which player you think best fits the provided characters. It's simple but still leads to a good amount of fun, just make sure you ignore the competitive aspect. Playing competitively takes a lot of the fun out of the game here.

6/10

[h1] Joke Boat [/h1]

So this is probably the most controversial game in the pack. You select a joke set up (I like my sex like I like my ____) something to fill in the blank (sandwiches) and then you finish the joke with your own punchline (covered in mayonnaise.) Then your joke is put up against somebody else's joke, and people vote quiplash style. This game is great when it isn't too restrictive, and terrible when it is. Even when it's not, games like Quiplash, Champ'd Up, and Mad Verse City are almost always more appealing, at least to me.

6/10

[h1] Dictionarium [/h1]

So for some reason everybody I play with doesn't understand the rules, but I guess I can't blame them because nobody really plays this that much. You make up a gibberish word, define it, use it in a sentence, and hope it ends up being funny. The game has potential, and I think it's more consistently good compared to Joke Boat, but it still doesn't compare to jackbox's better comedy games. I do want to give the game credit for its Archive though, that's a really cool touch. I do like this game, it's just not great compared to other games.

7/10

[h1] Push the Button [/h1]

1-2 aliens are selected, and everyone else has to find out who they are by testing everyone. I'm not going to go into much detail, but the game is honestly really complicated. However, once you learn how to play, the game is a TON of fun, and a personal favorite of mine. Also no, I'm not making an Among Us joke.

9/10

Note: This review will be kinda bias due to my favorite game in the Jackbox lineup is in this pack.
Fast Version: Really good games to enjoy with family and/or friends, Trivia Murder Party 2 is the best (In my opinion)

Games:
Trivia Murder Party 2: Exactly like the original, the gameplay is similar to "You Don't Know Jack" but with murder... of course (and it is in a hotel now)! The max amount of players that can play at once (excluding the "Audience" player if your streaming) is 8, but you can play by yourself if you have no friends like me! Typically each match has 8 trivia questions and then starts if there is one player left before the final round. In the event there is more than one player left, the remaining players will do a final killing room minigame that will result in either everyone dying.... or one player survives and they move to the final round. After every trivia question, the players who answer wrong go to "The Killing Room". When you are in the Killing Room, you will have to do a random minigame to save your butt. However, all players who got the trivia right, will have a chance to "assist" the participant. In the final round players be sent to the hotel lobby, the alive player is then able to answer trivia that you have to select what answers are correct for the question given. When you get one right you move 1 space, if you get both right you move 2 spaces. However, ghosts (dead players) can play too, they get the same prompts as the alive player but with one other possible answer (alive players have two). Which means they can move up to 3 spaces. If a ghost gets to the same space as an alive player, the ghost steals the life of the (previously) alive player, allowing the ghost player (now alive) to escape. If you beat the final round, you escape and win! If no one does, everyone dies. At this point you can do a "Sequel" which is a fancy/funny way of saying "play again", if you start a "sequel" all players will be either a descendant of their previous selfs with the same name. There is a chance when doing a sequel that all the players will have "Not" before their name. In the event that you are streaming, you can allow your audience to play as well. The audience player does everything the normal players do, except they don't go to the killing room if they answer wrong. All audience members playing will answer the prompts, the majority voted answer is the one that the audience character chooses. The audience does participate in the final round and CAN win (but knowing Twitch chats, they most likely will lose. 
ps. Money doesn't really matter in this game, mainly if you escape you win.

Joke Boat: This is just Mad Verse City (In Jackbox Party Pack 5) but less complicated and you make a punchline and not a rhyme. It's fun, just make sure the people you play with are funny. 8 players max in a match.

Dictionarium (Hope I spelled that right): In this game players (up to 8) will be given the task to give a definition for a made up word. Then players will vote on who's definition they like most, after that they will create another made up word that means the same thing and vote on it. After all of that, players will create and vote on a sentence using the newly made up word. This game is fun for a couple of rounds, but it isn't near the best at all.

Role Models: In this game players (up to 8) will choose a subject (Like Scooby-Doo), then they will sort the others players in the "role" they fit in regarding the subject (ie: Karma is Shaggy). depending on if the role you selected for a player is what the majority selected, you will get points. This will go on for 2 more rounds, then players will tie up some loose ends in a minigame (another voting thing) and it ends. Winning isn't really important in this game, mainly you'll play this game to see what family and friends think of you.

Push the Button: Have you heard of the hit indie-game Amon-...... Just kidding! In this game players (up to 8) will either be an alien or human. Human players have the goal to eject the alien/aliens, be careful though, you only get one button each AND human players only have 1 eject in general. This means if you eject the wrong player/players you will lose. In order to figure out who is the alien/aliens, the captain will choose a random test that is provided and select 2 or more players to test. In a test, aliens get a prompt that is different from humans, but to combat this aliens can hack humans to have the same effect. Aliens win if players eject someone wrong. This game is fun with a lot of players, which the minimum is 4.

Jackbox Party Packs are great games to play with friends or family at parties, over Discord, or elsewhere if you're looking for something casual to bring a group of people together and have a good time. Party Pack 6 is one of the better packs.

Joke Boat: Submit prompts and answers to prompts quickly and then use said prompts and answers to create stand-up comedy jokes to present to each other. It's bad. Really bad. Don't try it. You're better off just making your own jokes to tell to each other.

Trivia Murder Party 2: The sequel to the original Trivia Murder Party where you have to answer absurd trivia questions or be forced to play minigames to FIGHT FOR YOUR LIFE. Keep your soul for as long as possible and gain an advantage when you try to finally escape the haunted hotel. Really fun, and don't feel bad if you don't know the answers ever. It's supposed to be that way, you're not expected to know most of these facts.

Push The Button: An alien has infiltrated your crew aboard a spaceship. Through a series of tests, determine who the alien is and vote them off the ship in time. Throughout the tests, aliens will receive different prompts and tasks in order to give them away, but aliens also have the option to hack other humans or themselves to gain an advantage and slip under detection. Very fun if you've got a good group of deceptive people.

Dictionarium: Make new words and definitions for absurd or funny concepts, and vote on the best results. Can be pretty fun, can be pretty boring, depends on how creative your friends are.

Role Models: It's like Buzzfeed Quizzes, but your friends pick your results for you. Given various categories like "80s TV Shows", "Breakfast Foods", and "Ways to Hide Your Genitals", you will determine which answer best fits each other player. Similar to Buzzfeed Quizzes, once you play once you tend to keep going for a while, but unlike Buzzfeed Quizzes, it's actually pretty fun.

TL;DR Probably the best Party Pack there is. Definitely pick it up for $25 or less. 8/10

Reviewing the game as a whole, through subcategory, and summary of each game. 

1.) [b]Trivia Murder Party 2[/b]: 
This is the second one in the series. The first one, in Jackbox Party 3, however it doesn't matter which one you play, this is definitely the better one of the two, imo. As titled, it is a Trivia game. Starting out, you are chosen at random, a voodoo doll. Based in a hotel, you progress through it as the game goes on. You are asked trivia (random genres and time eras) questions and given 4 multiple choice answers, to choose from. Whoever gets the answer wrong, gets sent to a random "hotel" room, containing deviant minigames to which, in some cases, the ones who had gotten the answers right, may participate. Whoever gets the activity/answer wrong, will be pronounced as 'dead'. The last standing doll 'alive' or the one with the most money, gets the first advantage In the final round. Answers in the final round, could vary between all the answers, to none. This can conclude to one winner, or possibly none, if nobody gets all the answers right in the end. 
👍Great for friends and/or family, not even necessarily having to know all the answers, still makes the game a fun game. Has a lot of re-play value, from variety.

2.) [b]Dictionarium[/b]: 
In the first round you create a word, and then a sentence for the word. Second round, you create a synonym for the word. And use that into a sentence. Lastly, you vote amongst those who are playing, the one you feel is best (be it clever, or funny, etc - depending on your party that you play with). 
👍Ranging anywhere from clever-minded individuals to immature good fun, this could be seen as a good game amongst friends and/or Family.

3.) [b]Push The Button[/b]: 
You start off in a ship that has been invaded by 'aliens'. The ship's system will test you and may or may not mislead your choices toward who is really an alien or not. If you cannot find the alien(s) by the end of the game, it's doom for the rest of the team. 
👍👎 This game is fun, but may vary by the party who is playing. May possibly lose re-play value, from repetition. 

4.) [b]Role Models[/b]: 
You start off by picking subcategories that may or may not relate anywhere from some of your peers, to none. You are given subcategories such as a television show, or types of food and choosing who belongs to where.  In some cases, where there are similarities between people, you are placed in a voting system, and whoever gets the most votes, claim that title. 
👍👎 This game is also fun, but it works best with people that you know personally or on a more closer level. Such as best friends and/or family. May possibly lose re-play value, from repetition. 


5.) [b]Joke Boat[/b]: 
You have a choice of choosing a "dummy" puppet and telling jokes with it. You are given categories, as well as sentences to 'fill in the blank' (it's kind of like madlibs, if you are familiar with that) You are also given a key phrase to choose at the end of each "joke". 
👍👎I feel this game is fun, but depending on your party, may or may not be funny to those you tell the jokes to. The more clever you are with wording on the jokes, you are golden in this game.

[b]Trivia Murder Party 2[/b] is the best trivia game of all time. That is saying a lot, especially considering the genre that Trivia Murder Party 2 competes in. Many trivia games not made by Jackbox aren't engaging enough to others to really be considered "a game". And I do love the trivia games made by Jackbox, but when it comes to making the best and most enjoyable trivia experience, nothing compares to [REDACTED]'s twisted games. Besides the obvious changes (the new setting, questions, visuals), there's new minigames and mysteries to unravel. The Pegs game makes the Pachinko Game from Super Mario Sunshine a joke...I mean unless you were unlucky to hit those dollar sign slots. Wait, did I say unlucky? Sorry, I meant to say, lucky to hit those skull slots. Skewers is fine, I haven't gotten the Quiplash minigame yet, but I assume it's going to be a blast, Dictation really puts my keyboard skills to good use, and we can't forget the best minigame of Trivia Murder Party 2. [i]The Loser Wheel[/i]! It's nobody's favorite minigame! Just like the original, the ending has everyone fights to escape the hotel, regardless of how much money you earned. But there's a new twist: you need to get every answer right in the category provided to you by [REDACTED] to escape. Otherwise, you won't leave and everyone can overtake you in many different ways. Then there are the mysterious left in the game, mostly related to what is given in the Gifts minigame. But I have yet to escape with a gift sadly. While YOU DON'T KNOW JACK may have been the king of trivia games for a long time, it's safe to say that Trivia Murder Party 2 has taken that spot. And while I think this is the best game from Pack 6...it's also in The Jackbox Party Starter so...

[b]PUSH! THE! BUTTON![/b] This is the game to get Pack 6 with, just alone. An alien has infiltrated your human ship and your goal is to find who they are using various tests from writing, opinions, choices, or drawing. Depending on your room size, you could have up to three aliens to deal with. This means that for a 10-player game, you'll have a lot to work through to catch the three aliens on the ship. But you can't just push the button once you find one alien (in games that have two or three aliens). You need to find all of them, and then PUSH! THE! BUTTON! Otherwise, you risk losing your button privileges as everyone needs to agree on who to eject. If you don't find the aliens on time, you run out of buttons, or you eject a human on accident, the aliens take over, the humans die, and the aliens win the game. I can't tell you how many times we get to a point where we eject two aliens, but also one human. I CAN'T TELL YOU HOW MANY TIMES I FELT PAIN WHEN THE ALIEN IS REVEALED. This game truly inspires the chaos within everyone, just from the how the aliens can trick people using hacks. These hacks range from getting the human prompt instead of the designated alien prompt, or getting the human an alien prompt. I was bamboozled, over and over again. And the mess of trying to eject somebody is really the pinnacle of madness. If Summ is reading this, I just want to let you know how fucking dare you jinx me...not once, not even twice anymore, but three times! You maniac!!! /j All joking aside, this is the best game from Pack 6 if you're not counting Trivia Murder Party 2 in light of The Jackbox Party Starter.

[b]Role Models[/b] was nice. It's not a great game by any means, but it's pretty solid once I got a grip. Given a topic ranging from U.S. states to pop culture categories, it's up to you to guess where your peers are that they would associate with that role. If a majority agrees, the person gets that role, and if there's a tie, there's an additional test to be made to determine where that somebody is. Once the testing is done, your personality is given, and the titles given can be hilarious to read. For instance, I got the role "Foolish Painful Cowboy" based on the tests I was given. It's nice to have a game where we can sit back for once from all the trivia and aliens nonsense and try to take a turn to figure out our personality based on Winnie the Pooh characters, or Shopping Mall stores. And I feel this is severely underrated imo, even moreso than Blather 'Round. Not everyone talks about this game in regards to Pack 6, they're more focused on Trivia Murder Party 2, Push the Button, or Joke Boat. Dictionarium's only note is that it takes the shortest to play, but nobody has anything of note with Role Models. It has nothing special to share that nobody takes a glance until someone who has played it suggests it. And that's a shame! I like the concept and while I think the categories can be iffy, it's still great to try to get a good clue as to what your friends are personality-wise, and a great icebreaker at that. It's not one of the greatest, but it was fun and enjoyable.

Speaking of [b]Dictionarium[/b]...it was a game. Given a mumbo jumbo word, it's your goal to write the definition, synonym, and example. What's neat is that the winner answers will stay as a permanent entry in your game. That's really cool! It's also the shortest game as I mentioned. So...yeah...I'm going to be real here: this is just really boring and iffy to work a topic off. The music is...fine. The visuals are actually really cool. But it's not a game I want to play for Pack 6 alone.

A personal aesop, if a ship gets too bad to deal with, you gotta let that sink, man. That's how I feel with [b]Joke Boat[/b]. You are very limited to crack a good joke or two because much of what you have is mad libbed as heck. This may work for Mad Verse City, since you get two lines to write anything, but you are very limited to present a joke encapsulated in a template. I've given praises to presentation games like Talking Points given how I can be energetic and stuff, and I've also really loved games like Job Job, which while limiting, is still great because you get a good opportunity to write the most broken text and still create the best laughs. How am I suppose to play this game? You cannot tell me I need to present something about how to screw a lightbulb. I've gotten last place...twice. This is not something I should be having in a Jackbox game. Even my most hated Jackbox game didn't get me to complaining to everyone that they hated me and my jokes. I'm serious, this game gave me such a headache after playing it that I really cannot enjoy this as I should anymore. You can't make a game where the jokes have to be mad libbed. There's no way to be funny with a mad lib. Maybe it's just me being a bit pessimistic or salty, I don't fucking know. Whatever it is, I am not interested to play this piece of shit ever again. It's not going to get me on my toes like my other hated Jackbox game, but it is not good.

Overall, what a disappointment. With one game that is really, really good but can also be found in Starter, and something that I consider better than Among Us. But three games that don't hit the mark. Like damn, this game is worth it for Push the Button, but it cannot sell the other games. If you don't own Starter, fine, you can buy this for Trivia Murder Party 2. But just know this is my least played Pack overall, and I just started playing it just for Push the Button. I'm serious, Pack 6's only selling point is Push the Button. So um...just skip this Pack. If you do want Push the Button, please buy it, but I wouldn't blame you if you wanted to do Among Us instead.

Trivia Murder Party 2 is a huge improvement over the first iteration. The original game was something that neither me or my friends ever wanted to play after the first time we tried it due to feeling like a slog to get through. 2's pace has been quickened up by a substantial amount. It's still kind of reliant on whether you get the trivia questions themselves or not, a lot of which are still beyond obscure and strange, but the addition of removing U.S.-centric questions is helpful. This is one of the good games on this pack.

Role Models is really fun, but a strange one because it's not a competitive game like the usual Jackbox game is. It's just about assigning roles to your friends, leading to some goofy results that got my group laughing pretty hard. The problem is just that the game's scoring system feels out of place; this game doesn't work for trying to get a better score over your friends.

Joke Boat is a game with a lot of potential but I don't think it quite reaches it. It's heavily reliant on your group's humor which can lead to [i]really[/i] hit and miss results. It feels too easy to get screwed over by either bad options from your friends giving up or just a bad setup from the game itself. This one is going depend on who you play with.

Dictionarium has [i]so much potential[/i] and it just utterly disappoints me that it's the worst game in the package. Making up words and their definitions sounds hilarious, but the way it's structured just ruins any potential. Why aren't the word game or phrase game options right at the main menu, instead of being locked to the first-joining VIP? Why does the word-game just make everyone compete over one single word when it could be more fun with a Quiplash-like structure? I don't know. This one just hurts to play.

Push The Button is the selling point. The best way I can describe it is that it's like Trouble in Terrorist Town or things akin to it: there are several people in your ship who are not who they say they are, and you have to figure it out by testing each person on the ship in various ways. But even those who are innocent can be screwed over by the aliens, leading to a lot of goofy yelling matches between your friends. The only issues with this game is that the Bioscanner is the worst option because basically nobody will get it right, even those who are innocent. That, and the audience option just doesn't really work for this game. Push The Button requires a group of friends sitting in a Discord call, not for Twitch streamers and random strangers.

I just don't think Party Pack 6 reaches the heights that 3 and 4 do. I already see myself just opening those up again for Quiplash, Fibbage, Tee K.O, Monster Seeking Monster, and more. 6 is disappointing. If you don't already have at least 3 or 4, I'll recommend those first over 6.
